open_issues: Boundary records in extraction_boundary_report.json: records the N draws write (per attempt, ladder checkpoints) are appended as they happen, so their ORDER across draws is completion order and they carry no draw number (they carried none before either). The ensemble report, summary and attempt log are in draw order with draw numbers. Kept on purpose: a per-draw buffer would delay the ladder checkpoint that must be on disk BEFORE a long LLM call. current_draw() is available if the boundary record should carry a draw number.
A non-PipelineFailure exception in one draw waits for the other draws to finish before propagating (cannot cancel a running HTTP call); sequentially they would never have started.
rate_limit_analysis: No shared limiter and no provider concurrency cap exist in src/t2pw/llm. client.chat_detailed retries per call: up to LLM_MAX_RETRIES=8, exponential backoff min(1*2^attempt, 20) s on RateLimitError/timeouts/APIError, plus LLM_CALL_SPACING=0.35 s sleep after each call. Each draw thread backs off independently, so a 429 on one draw does not stall the others and does not defeat the backoff. Pool = N (N=3 in paper runs), so at most N Stage-1 requests are in flight per run; the batch driver already runs legs in threads, so concurrent calls are not new. The web path caps each request at 720 s (LLM_CALL_CAP_SECONDS) on its own worker thread; unaffected. If the provider later needs a cap, add it as a semaphore around chat_detailed in client.py. CORRECTION: the batch driver runs legs as child processes, not threads, so N Stage-1 requests in flight per run IS new load. 429 backoff is now jittered (x0.5..1.0, never above the old value) so draws that hit a 429 together do not retry in lockstep.
